name: Alexandre M. Bayen
title: Liao-Cho Professor of Engineering; Associate Provost for Moffett Field Program Development
department: Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences; Civil and Environmental Engineering
fitReason: Substantive learning-to-control deployed into real traffic; application scope is vehicle longitudinal control rather than general manipulation.

physicalEvidence.summary: The 2024 primary manuscript, published in the February 2025 IEEE Control Systems Magazine issue and explained by the authors in March 2025, documents RL controllers on 100 Nissan Rogue cars during the November 2022 I-24 MegaVanderTest. Neural policies trained on trajectory-based simulation were exported to ONNX/ROS and controlled adaptive-cruise speed settings with safety limits. Vehicles remained partially automated with human drivers; this is not driverless perception-to-steering control. Physical deployment is consortium hardware from 2022, not a newly demonstrated Berkeley fleet or guaranteed 2027 access. Physical credit is capped at 20.

name: Stephanie Gil
title: John L. Loeb Associate Professor of Engineering and Applied Sciences; REACT Lab PI
department: Computer Science, School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
fitReason: Substantive probabilistic/model-based AI for actual field autonomy; more rollout planning and sensing fusion than deep learned visuomotor policies.

physicalEvidence.summary: December 2025 primary paper integrates Gaussian-mixture acoustic separation, particle-filter beliefs and a model-based RL/rollout navigation framework with a Holybro S500/Pixhawk UAV. Dominica trials achieved two whale rendezvous within 200 m. Table 1 explicitly keeps boat maneuvers, belief-candidate selection and takeoff manual in the sea trials; waypoint navigation was autonomous. Autonomous takeoff/selection and larger success-rate studies were simulation. Current REACT roster lists coauthors Ninad Jadhav, Hammad Izhar and Karen Li, establishing directed-group linkage; former coauthor Sushmita Bhattacharya is now an alumna. This is not a neural end-to-end flight policy.

name: Miroslav Pajic
title: Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering; Cyber-Physical Systems Lab lead
department: Electrical and Computer Engineering; Computer Science; Mechanical Engineering and Materials Science
fitReason: Strong substantive AI/control profile with real heterogeneous robot coordination and active offline-to-online RL methods.

physicalEvidence.summary: LLM-MCoX September 2025 primary preprint executes centralized multimodal-LLM waypoint assignment on an actual Unitree Go2 and customized X500 quadrotor, both carrying Livox Mid360 LiDAR, in an indoor target-search trial. The planner incorporates a directional language hint; local SLAM Toolbox/Nav2 handle geometry and motion. A central PC replans on a 20-second horizon. Six-robot efficiency gains are simulation, not the two-robot physical trial. Current CPSL roster includes first author Ruiyang Wang and coauthors Hao-Lun Hsu, David Hunt, Jiwoo Kim and Shaocheng Luo, establishing directed-group linkage. April 2026 SAGR benchmarks are Habitat simulation and not additional physical execution.

shortVisit.summary: Current lab explicitly recruits PhD students and postdocs. Current Duke master’s mentees and historical outside undergraduate visitors are not a current external-master’s short-visit invitation. No qualifying eight-week/2027 offer verified.

scoreReasons.fit: Learned high-level robot planning plus active safe/offline-to-online RL; no claim the LLM is a low-level motor controller.
